docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Super Admin Panel is the centralized management interface for the Recon AI reconciliation platform. It serves as the nerve center for platform operators, enabling them to control every aspect of the multi-tenant environment.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The primary goal of this panel is to allow superusers to:

  • Configure System-Wide Settings: Manage global parameters that affect all tenants.
  • Manage Tenants: Onboard, approve, and configure client organizations.
  • Control Access: Define roles and permissions to ensure secure operations.
  • Define Logic: Create and maintain the reusable rules that drive reconciliation.
  • Oversee Subscriptions: Manage billing tiers and feature access for clients.

docs.title: Intended Users
docs.text:
This documentation is specifically written for:

  • Super Admins: Users with full system access.
  • Platform Operators: Technical staff managing the daily health of the platform.
  • Internal Support & Ops Teams: Staff responsible for onboarding and troubleshooting client issues.

docs.title: Navigation Structure
docs.text: The admin panel is organized into logical sections via the left-hand Sidebar Menu. The menu is visually split into "header" sections (gray text) and "links" (white text).

docs.title: Menu Sections
docs.text:
1. Dashboard: The main landing page.
  2. Clients Management:
    • Clients: Manage tenant organizations.
    • Domains: Manage URL entry points.
  3. Base Configuration:
    • Modules: System capabilities.
    • Permissions: Access control definitions.
    • Rule Components: Reusable logic blocks.
    • Subscription Plans: Commercial tier definitions.

docs.title: Access & Authentication
docs.text: Data security and access control are paramount in the Recon AI platform. The Super Admin panel is secured via a robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system, ensuring that only authorized personnel can make system-wide configurations.

docs.title: Admin URL
docs.text:
All administrative actions are performed through the centralized admin portal:

  • Primary URL: https://devapi-recon.dharsi.ai/admin/

!!! note "Environment Check" Please confirm you are accessing the correct environment (Dev, Staging, or Prod) as the URL prefix will vary for each.

docs.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
docs.text:
Access to the Super Admin panel is strictly restricted to users with the superuser or superadmin role. Standard users and client-level administrators cannot access this interface.

  • Authentication Method: Secure login via email and password (or SSO if configured).
  • Session Management: Sessions are timed out automatically after periods of inactivity to prevent unauthorized access.

docs.title: User Context
docs.text:
Once logged in, the system provides visual indicators of your current session:

  • Sidebar: Displays the logged-in user's email address at the bottom for quick verification.
  • Profile Menu: Located in the top-right corner, allowing access to:
    • Account Settings
    • Password Change
    • Logout

!!! warning "Security Best Practice" Always log out of your admin session when stepping away from your workstation to maintain system security.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Clients represent organizations or tenants using the Recon AI platform. Whenever a new client registers, it is automatically listed in the Clients table and requires approval by a superuser before becoming fully operational.

docs.title: Client Registration, Approval & Rejection Flow
docs.text:
1. A client completes registration on the Recon AI platform.
  2. An email notification is sent to the Super User at support@dharsi.ai.
  3. The client appears in the Clients table with:
  4. Approval Status: Pending Approval
  5. A Super User reviews the client details.
  6. The Super User clicks the Approve action.
  7. A confirmation popup appears with options to:
  8. Approve the client
  9. Reject the client (with reason)
  10. Based on the action taken:
  11. The client status is updated
  12. An automated email notification is sent to the client

docs.title: Clients Listing Page
docs.text:
Navigation

Admin Panel → Clients → Clients

Purpose - View all registered clients - Filter and search client records - Approve or reject pending clients - Access detailed client configuration

docs.title: Clients Table Fields
docs.text: Field Description Name Client or tenant name Schema Name Database schema associated with the client Status Operational state of the client Timezone Default timezone for the client Default Currency Primary currency used by the client Approval Status Pending Approval / Approved / Rejected Action Approve button for pending clients

docs.title: Filters & Search
docs.text:
Superusers can filter and search clients using: - Status - Timezone - Default Currency - Approval Status - Keyword search

This helps efficiently manage large numbers of tenants.

docs.title: Approve Action
docs.text:
• Clicking Approve opens a confirmation popup.
  • On confirmation:
  • Client approval status changes to Approved
  • The client becomes eligible for subscription and full access
  • An approval email is automatically sent to the client

docs.title: Reject Action
docs.text:
• Selecting Reject prompts the Super User to provide a reason for rejection.
  • On rejection:
  • Client approval status changes to Rejected
  • The client remains inactive
  • A rejection email with the provided reason is sent to the client

This ensures transparency and proper communication with the client.

docs.title: Client Detail View
docs.text:
Clicking on a client opens the Client Detail Page, where the superuser can view and manage all client-specific settings.

Navigation

Admin Panel → Clients → Clients → [Client Name]

docs.title: Client Detail Tabs
docs.text: The Client Detail page is divided into multiple tabs for clarity and ease of management.

docs.title: 1. Basic Information
docs.text:
Purpose Defines the core identity and operational state of the client.

Fields - Client Name - Schema Name - Industry - Status (Active / Inactive) - Approval Status - Allocated Storage (GB)

Available Actions - Save - Save and continue editing - Save and add another - Delete - View change history

docs.title: 2. Subscription Details
docs.text:
Purpose Used to assign and manage the client’s subscription plan.

Includes - Subscription Plan selection (e.g., Free Trial, Paid Plans) - Subscription Start Date and Time - Subscription End Date and Time

Behavior - Determines which modules and features the client can access - Enforces plan validity and expiration - Subscription changes take effect based on configured dates

docs.title: 3. Regional Settings
docs.text:
Purpose Defines regional and localization preferences for the client.

Fields - Timezone - Default Currency

These settings affect: - Data processing - Reporting - Reconciliation timelines - Financial calculations

docs.title: 4. Audit Info
docs.text:
Purpose Provides auditability and traceability for client-related changes.

Displays - Created At timestamp - Last Updated At timestamp

Audit information ensures compliance, governance, and accountability.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard serves as the command center for the Super Admin. It is designed to provide "at-a-glance" visibility into the health and status of the Recon AI platform.

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text: Upon logging in, administrators are greeted with the Dashboard, which is strictly organized into clean functional areas to maximize efficiency.

docs.title: Visual Layout
docs.text:
The interface is divided into three primary zones:

  1. Sidebar (Left)

    • Dark gray background.
    • Contains the primary navigation menu.
    • Shows the active user (email) and organization logo (dharisi Recon AI).

  2. Operations Center (Middle)

    • Contains grouped "Cards" for quick access to core entities.
    • Clients Card: Quick links to Clients and Domains.
    • Base Card: Quick links to Modules, Permissions, Rule components, and Subscription Plans.
    • Action Buttons:
      • Add : Green button to immediately create a new record.
      • Change : Blue button to go to the list/edit view.

  3. Recent Actions Timeline (Right)

    • A vertical timeline feed on the right side of the screen.
    • Displays a chronological history of administrative actions.

docs.title: Breadcrumb Navigation
docs.text: Located at the top of the content area (e.g., Home › Dashboard), this helps you track your location within the site hierarchy.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Domains define the logical hostnames or URLs mapped to specific tenants. They allow the Recon AI platform to identify which client environment to load based on the URL being accessed.

docs.title: Domains Listing Page
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Clients → Domains

Purpose - View all registered hostnames and their associated tenants. - Identify primary domains for multi-domain clients. - Perform bulk actions (e.g., deleting multiple domain records).

docs.title: Domains Table Fields
docs.text: Field Description Domain The specific hostname/URL (e.g., tenant-v1.devapi-recon.dharsi.ai). Tenant The Client Name and its corresponding Schema Name in parentheses. Is primary A visual indicator (green checkmark) signifying if this is the main domain for the tenant.

docs.title: Filters & Search
docs.text:
• Search: A dedicated search bar to find domains by hostname.
  • Is primary Filter: A dropdown menu to filter the list by "Primary" or "Non-Primary" status.
  • Add Domain: A green action button to register a new hostname.

docs.title: Domain Detail View
docs.text:
Clicking on a specific domain hostname opens the Change Domain interface. This view uses a tabbed layout to separate configuration.

Navigation Admin Panel → Clients → Domains → [Domain Name]

docs.title: 1. Domain Details
docs.text:
Purpose Defines the hostname and its priority.

Fields - Domain (Required): The full hostname string. This field is mandatory (marked with a red asterisk). - Is primary: A checkbox. When selected, this domain is treated as the primary entry point for the associated tenant.

docs.title: 2. Linked Tenant
docs.text: Purpose Used to associate the domain with a specific registered Client/Tenant in the system.

docs.title: Available Actions (Right Sidebar)
docs.text: The following actions are available when adding or editing a domain: - Save: Commits changes and returns to the domain list. - Delete: Removes the domain entry from the system. - Save and add another: Saves the current domain and opens a fresh "Add Domain" form. - Save and continue editing: Saves changes and keeps the current page open. - History: Opens an audit log showing which admin users modified the domain and when.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Modules represent functional capabilities of the platform. They are used as a group of permissions for respective applications in Recon AI.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Data Ingestion
  • Reconciliation Engine
  • Risk & Anomaly Detection
  • Reporting & Analytics

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: • Enable or disable per client

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Efficient platform operation requires visibility and governance. The Operations tools provide the necessary oversight for Super Admins.

docs.title: Recent Actions Timeline
docs.text: The Recent Actions panel is prominently displayed on the right side of the Dashboard as a vertical timeline. It provides a real-time feed of administrative activity.

docs.title: Visual Guide
docs.text:
The timeline uses specific visual cues to help you scan information quickly:

  • Icons:
    • :pencil: Pencil Icon (Blue Background): Indicates an edit or change to an existing record.
    • :heavy_plus_sign: Plus Icon (Green Background): Indicates a new creation (if applicable).
  • Metadata:
    • Relative Time: e.g., "1 month, 1 week ago".
    • Entity Name: The specific object that was modified (e.g., Match Criteria or test company).
    • Action Summary: A brief description of what happened (e.g., Changed Subscription end date or Changed Component json).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Auditability: Retrace the steps leading to a configuration issue.
  • Accountability: Identify who made specific changes.
  • Transparency: Keep the entire ops team aligned on recent system updates.

docs.title: The "Add" Operation
docs.text: Used to instantiate new records in the database. - Clients: Onboarding a new tenant manually. - Domains: Registering a new entry point. - Rule Components: Extending the platform's logic library. - Permissions: Defining new granular access controls.

docs.title: The "Change" Operation
docs.text: Used to modify existing configurations. - Updates: Changing a client's Subscription Plan. - Corrections: Fixing a typo in a domain name. - Status Changes: Approving or rejecting a client. - Configuration: Enabling or disabling Modules for a client.

docs.title: Governance & Best Practices
docs.text:
To maintain a healthy platform environment, adhere to the following guidelines:

  1. Least Privilege: Limit the number of users with superuser status. Only assign it to those who absolutely need it.
  2. Validation: Always test new Rule Components in a staging environment before deploying them to production/all clients.
  3. Subscription Management: Assign subscription plans before enabling a client to ensure they don't access restricted features for free.
  4. Monitoring: regularly review the Recent Actions timeline to spot unintended or suspicious configuration changes.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Permissions control user and role access across the platform. They allow specific actions (read, write, update, delete) to be granularly assigned to modules.

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text:
• Role-based permissions
  • Module-level access
  • Action-based control

docs.title: Permissions Listing Page
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Base → Permissions

Purpose - View all defined permissions in the system. - Search for specific permissions by module or code.

docs.title: Permissions Table Fields
docs.text: Field Description Code The unique identifier for the permission (e.g., RECONCILIATION_RESULT_VIEW). Label A human-readable name for the permission. Module The module this permission belongs to (e.g., Reconciliation Result, Pipeline Management).

docs.title: Permission Detail View
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Base → Permissions → [Permission Name]

Purpose - View and edit the details of a specific permission.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
• Code: The system identifier for the permission (Required).
  • Label: The display name for the permission (Required).
  • Description: A brief explanation of what the permission allows (e.g., "Can view reconciliation results").

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Client A tenant organization using the Recon AI platform. Data is siloed per client. Domain A logical subdivision or entry point associated with a client. Used for routing. Module A functional capability of the system (e.g., Reconciliation, Reporting). Permission A granular rule controlling access (read, write, etc.) to specific modules. Rule Component A reusable unit of logic used to construct reconciliation rules. Subscription Plan A tiered package defining feature access, usage limits, and pricing. Schema The database namespace isolated for a specific client.

docs.title: Future Enhancements (Roadmap)
docs.text:
These features are planned for upcoming releases:

  • Advanced Audit Logging: Deeper insights into specific field-level changes.
  • Admin Analytics Dashboard: Usage statistics for the platform (e.g., total volume processed across all clients).
  • Role-Scoped Admin Views: Restricted admin access (e.g., "Support User" who can view but not edit).
  • Bulk Management: Tools to update multiple clients or rules simultaneously.
  • Approval Workflows: Multi-step approval processes for critical changes.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Reusable components used to define reconciliation and matching logic. These components are the building blocks for creating flexible and complex reconciliation rules.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Match Types: Defines relationships (e.g., One-to-One, Many-to-Many).
  • Match Conditions: Logical conditions for matching.
  • Tolerances: Allowable differences in matching (e.g., amount or date variance).
  • Match Criteria: Specific fields or attributes to match on.

docs.title: Rule Components Listing Page
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Base → Rule Components

Purpose - View all available rule components. - Manage existing components (edit, delete). - Create new rule components.

docs.title: Table Fields
docs.text:
• Name: The name of the rule component (e.g., Match Types).
  • Is active: Status indicator (green checkmark for active).
  • Updated at: Timestamp of the last modification.

docs.title: Rule Component Detail View
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Base → Rule Components → [Component Name]

Purpose - Configure the specific logic and schema for a rule component using the JSON editor.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
• Name: The display name of the component.
  • Description: textual description of what the component does.
  • Component JSON: The core configuration field. This JSON object defines the properties, types, and logic for the component (e.g., defining "one-to-one" or "many-to-many" options for a Match Type).
  • Is active: Checkbox to enable or disable the component.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Subscription plans define feature access and usage limits for clients. They allow you to tier your service offerings (e.g., Free Trial, Pro, Enterprise) and control resource consumption.

docs.title: Subscription Plans Listing Page
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Base → Subscription Plans

Purpose - View all available subscription plans. - Check the status/terms of each plan (Trial status, Duration, User limits). - Create or modify plans.

docs.title: Table Fields
docs.text:
• Name: The display name of the plan (e.g., "Free Trial").
  • Is trial: Indicates if this is a trial plan (Green checkmark = Yes).
  • Duration number: The numeric value for the plan's validity (e.g., 14).
  • Duration unit: The unit of time for the duration (e.g., Days, Months).
  • User limit: The maximum number of users allowed under this plan.
  • Subscription id: Unique identifier for the plan in the system.

docs.title: Subscription Plan Detail View
docs.text:
Navigation Admin Panel → Base → Subscription Plans → [Plan Name]

Purpose - Configure the specific terms, limits, and identifiers for a subscription plan.

docs.title: 1. General
docs.text:
Basic identity configuration for the plan.

  • Name: The plan name shown to users.
  • Is trial: Checkbox to mark this as a trial plan.
  • Subscription id: A unique system ID (e.g., FREE_TRIAL).

docs.title: 2. Plan Details
docs.text:
Configuration of limits and validity periods.

  • Duration number: Length of time the plan is valid.
  • Duration unit: Time unit (Days, Weeks, Months, Years).
  • User limit: Maximum number of user accounts permitted for a client on this plan.
